heroHeadline: Russian Drones Pound Kyiv Hours After Zelenskyy-Trump Energy Ceasefire Talks
heroSubtitle: Hours after President Zelenskyy met President Trump at the UN General Assembly on September 22 to discuss an energy ceasefire, Russia struck Kyiv with jet-powered drones on September 23, hitting petrol stations, the historic Shayba railway market and rail infrastructure, killing 2 and injuring 40+; separately, Russian aerial bombs killed 5 and trapped children under rubble in Oleksandrivka, Donetsk Oblast. Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt strikes on energy infrastructure, but Kyiv said it was not informed of any such deal. On September 22, a nationwide Russian missile and drone barrage killed 8 and wounded 37 across seven oblasts, including a strike on the Interpipe plant in Dnipro, while Ukrainian drones struck the Samara and Ufa oil refineries deep inside Russia. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,522,440 by September 23, per the Ukrainian General Staff.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
